simple.meaning: נָאַק (nâʼaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to groan.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Job, Ezekiel, beginning at Job 24:12. The surrounding contexts include kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָאַק (H5008) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נָאַק (nâʼaq) / H5008 is traced through Job 24:12, Ezekiel 30:24 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H5008. naaq נָאַק verb groan (Aramaic נְאַק (rare)); — Qal Perfect וְנָאַק consecutive Ezek 30:24 with accusative of congnate meaning with verb figurative of Pharaoh before king of Babylon (emendation Co see נַאֲקָה Imperfect Job 24:12 יִנְאָ֑קוּ .

occurrences.englishText: From out of the populous city, men groan.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, and put my sword in his hand; but I will break the arms of Pharaoh, and he will groan before the king of Babylon with the groaning of a mortally wounded man.
